subject: ela
intro: Each passage below contains more than one usage problem, or a subtle one, involving pronoun case, intensive pronouns, shifts in number or person, or vague references. Read carefully, decide what the writer means, and rewrite each passage so it follows standard English. Then explain the conventions you applied.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Me and Devon signed up for the science fair last week. Us two have been collecting data on plant growth every morning. Our teacher said that him and the judges were impressed by our notes.' Rewrite the passage so every pronoun follows standard English, and identify the case error you fixed in each sentence.
items.answer: 'Devon and I signed up for the science fair last week. We two have been collecting data on plant growth every morning. Our teacher said that he and the judges were impressed by our notes.' Each subject needs the subjective case: 'Devon and I' and 'We two' are subjects of their sentences, and 'he and the judges' is the subject of the clause 'that he and the judges were impressed.'

steps: Sentence 1: 'Me and Devon' is the subject performing the action 'signed up,' so use the subjective 'I.' Standard order also places the other person first: 'Devon and I signed up.'
Sentence 2: 'Us two' is the subject doing the collecting, so the subjective 'We two have been collecting' is correct.
Sentence 3: 'him and the judges' is the subject of the clause 'that ___ were impressed,' so use the subjective 'he and the judges were impressed.'
Test each compound by dropping the other noun: 'I signed up,' 'We have been collecting,' 'he was impressed' all sound right, confirming the subjective case.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'The coach handed the trophies to Jordan and I after the final game. Between you and I, that win meant everything to the team. The whole crowd cheered for we players as we left the field.' Rewrite the passage so each pronoun uses the correct case, and explain why the objective case is needed in each spot.
items.answer: 'The coach handed the trophies to Jordan and me after the final game. Between you and me, that win meant everything to the team. The whole crowd cheered for us players as we left the field.' Each corrected pronoun is the object of a preposition ('to,' 'between,' 'for'), so the objective case (me, us) is required.

steps: Sentence 1: 'to Jordan and I' is the object of the preposition 'to,' so use the objective 'to Jordan and me.' Drop the other name: 'handed the trophies to me' confirms it.
Sentence 2: 'Between you and I' is an overcorrection; the pronoun follows the preposition 'between,' so it must be objective: 'between you and me.'
Sentence 3: 'for we players' follows the preposition 'for,' so use the objective 'for us players.'
The final 'we left the field' is correct because 'we' is the subject of that clause, doing the leaving.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Myself and Priya organized the food drive at our school. The principal thanked Priya and myself in the morning announcements. We were proud that we ourselves had collected over a thousand cans.' Rewrite the passage so the pronouns follow standard English, and explain the difference between a subject pronoun, an object pronoun, and an intensive pronoun.
items.answer: 'Priya and I organized the food drive at our school. The principal thanked Priya and me in the morning announcements. We were proud that we ourselves had collected over a thousand cans.' A subject uses 'I,' an object uses 'me,' and 'ourselves' is an intensive pronoun that correctly emphasizes 'we.'

steps: Sentence 1: 'Myself' cannot serve as a subject; the subject of 'organized' must be 'I,' giving 'Priya and I organized.'
Sentence 2: 'myself' cannot be an object replacing 'me'; 'thanked Priya and me' uses the objective case after the verb.
Sentence 3: 'we ourselves' is correct because 'ourselves' is an intensive pronoun emphasizing the subject 'we' and can be removed without changing the basic meaning.
Rule: an intensive pronoun (myself, ourselves) only adds emphasis to a noun or pronoun already in the sentence; it can never stand in for a subject or object.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'When a student joins the robotics club, they should bring their own safety goggles. You will also need a notebook for sketching designs. If a member misses a meeting, they must email the captain.' Rewrite the passage so that pronoun number and person stay consistent in the third person, and explain the shifts you corrected.
items.answer: 'When students join the robotics club, they should bring their own safety goggles. They will also need a notebook for sketching designs. If members miss a meeting, they must email the captain.' Making the antecedents plural ('students,' 'members') keeps the number consistent, and changing 'You' to 'They' keeps the person consistent in the third person throughout.

steps: Sentence 1 begins with the singular 'a student' but uses plural 'they/their.' Make the antecedent plural: 'When students join... they should bring their own goggles.'
Sentence 2 shifts from third person to second person with 'You.' Keep third person: 'They will also need a notebook.'
Sentence 3 again pairs singular 'a member' with plural 'they.' Make it plural: 'If members miss a meeting, they must email the captain.'
Consistent practice: pick one number and one person for a set of related sentences and hold to it so the reader is not jolted between singular/plural or third/second person.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Maria told Jen that she had qualified for the regional spelling bee. After the assembly, Jen ran to her parents to share the news. Everyone could see how excited she was.' The writer intends to say that Jen qualified. Rewrite the passage so the pronoun references are clear, and explain why the original is vague.
items.answer: 'Maria told Jen that Jen had qualified for the regional spelling bee. After the assembly, Jen ran to her parents to share the news. Everyone could see how excited Jen was.' In the original, 'she' could refer to either Maria or Jen; replacing 'she' with the name 'Jen' removes the ambiguity and matches the intended meaning.

steps: Identify the ambiguity: in 'Maria told Jen that she had qualified,' the pronoun 'she' has two possible antecedents, Maria and Jen.
Use the intended meaning: the passage says Jen ran to share the news and Jen was excited, so the writer means Jen qualified.
Replace the vague 'she' with the name: 'Maria told Jen that Jen had qualified.'
Check the last sentence: 'how excited she was' is also unclear, so name the person: 'how excited Jen was.' Naming the antecedent fixes both vague references.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'The hikers reached the summit just as the storm clouds rolled in. It was the highlight of the whole trip. Now they tell everyone about it whenever they get the chance.' The pronoun 'It' in the second sentence has no clear noun to refer to. Rewrite the passage so 'It' has a clear antecedent, and explain the problem.
items.answer: 'The hikers reached the summit just as the storm clouds rolled in. Reaching the summit was the highlight of the whole trip. Now they tell everyone about it whenever they get the chance.' The original 'It' had no clear noun to point to, so replacing 'It' with the phrase 'Reaching the summit' gives the pronoun idea a clear referent.

steps: Find the vague pronoun: 'It was the highlight' does not point to any single noun in the first sentence.
Decide what 'It' means from context: the highlight was the event of reaching the summit.
Replace the vague 'It' with the noun phrase it stands for: 'Reaching the summit was the highlight of the whole trip.'
Rule: a pronoun must have a clear, stated antecedent. When no noun fits, name the idea directly instead of leaving a floating 'it' or 'this.'

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Me and my cousins built a treehouse over the summer. My uncle helped my cousins and I carry the wood up the ladder. When a person builds something with their family, you remember it forever.' Rewrite the passage to fix the case errors and the shift in person, and explain each correction.
items.answer: 'My cousins and I built a treehouse over the summer. My uncle helped my cousins and me carry the wood up the ladder. When people build something with their family, they remember it forever.' The first sentence needs the subject 'My cousins and I,' the second needs the object 'my cousins and me,' and the last sentence must stay in the third person with the plural 'people... they.'

steps: Sentence 1: 'Me and my cousins' is the subject of 'built,' so use 'My cousins and I built.'
Sentence 2: 'helped my cousins and I' uses the pronoun as the object of 'helped,' so use the objective 'my cousins and me.'
Sentence 3: it shifts from 'a person... their' (third person singular) to 'you' (second person). Make it consistent third person plural: 'When people build... they remember it forever.'
Drop-the-noun test confirms 'I built' and 'helped me' are correct.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Our band director gave clear feedback to the trumpet section and we. Him and the drum line practiced an extra hour each day. By the concert, everyone agreed that them players had improved the most.' Rewrite the passage so all three pronouns use the correct case, and explain the rule behind each fix.
items.answer: 'Our band director gave clear feedback to the trumpet section and us. He and the drum line practiced an extra hour each day. By the concert, everyone agreed that those players had improved the most.' 'Us' is the object of the preposition 'to,' 'He' is the subject of 'practiced,' and 'them' cannot modify a noun, so the demonstrative 'those' is used.

steps: Sentence 1: 'to the trumpet section and we' follows the preposition 'to,' so use the objective 'us.'
Sentence 2: 'Him and the drum line practiced' is the subject of 'practiced,' so use the subjective 'He and the drum line practiced.'
Sentence 3: 'them players' misuses an object pronoun as an adjective before a noun. Standard English uses the demonstrative 'those players.'
Each fix matches the pronoun's job: object after a preposition, subject before a verb, and a determiner before a noun.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'After the long rehearsal, the actors and the director reviewed the script. They decided it needed a new ending. Then they thanked them for staying late.' The pronouns 'they' and 'them' are confusing because they could point to either group. The writer means the director thanked the actors. Rewrite the last sentence so the references are clear, and explain the ambiguity.
items.answer: 'After the long rehearsal, the actors and the director reviewed the script. Everyone decided it needed a new ending. Then the director thanked the actors for staying late.' The original 'they thanked them' was unclear because both 'they' and 'them' could mean the actors or the director; naming each group removes the ambiguity.

steps: Identify the problem: in 'they thanked them,' both pronouns could refer to the actors or the director, so the reader cannot tell who thanked whom.
Use the intended meaning: the director thanked the actors.
Name the groups directly: 'the director thanked the actors for staying late.'
The earlier 'They decided' is also vague, so 'Everyone decided' clarifies that both the actors and the director agreed. Replacing pronouns with nouns resolves the confusion.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'If a writer wants to improve, you should read every day and keep a journal. A good author trusts their own voice. When they revise, a writer cuts the words you do not need.' Rewrite the passage so the number and person stay consistent throughout, and explain the shifts you removed.
items.answer: 'If writers want to improve, they should read every day and keep a journal. Good authors trust their own voice. When they revise, writers cut the words they do not need.' Using plural antecedents ('writers,' 'authors') and keeping every pronoun in the third person ('they,' not 'you') removes the shifts in both number and person.

steps: Sentence 1 shifts from singular third person 'a writer' to second person 'you.' Make it plural third person: 'If writers want to improve, they should read every day.'
Sentence 2: 'A good author' is singular but uses plural 'their.' Make it plural to agree: 'Good authors trust their own voice.'
Sentence 3 shifts again to 'you do not need.' Keep third person plural: 'writers cut the words they do not need.'
Choosing one consistent number and person across the passage keeps the writing smooth and standard.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'The museum guide herself led my brother and I through the dinosaur hall. She showed my brother and I a fossil that was millions of years old. Me and him could not stop talking about it.' Rewrite the passage to correct the case errors, and explain why the intensive pronoun 'herself' is already correct.
items.answer: 'The museum guide herself led my brother and me through the dinosaur hall. She showed my brother and me a fossil that was millions of years old. He and I could not stop talking about it.' 'My brother and me' is the object of the verbs 'led' and 'showed,' and 'He and I' is the subject of the last sentence. 'Herself' is already correct because it is an intensive pronoun emphasizing 'guide.'

steps: 'The guide herself led' is correct: 'herself' is an intensive pronoun adding emphasis to the subject 'guide,' and it can be removed without breaking the sentence.
Sentence 1: 'led my brother and I' uses the pronoun as the object of 'led,' so use the objective 'my brother and me.'
Sentence 2: 'showed my brother and I' is the object of 'showed,' so again use 'my brother and me.'
Sentence 3: 'Me and him' is the subject of 'could not stop,' so use the subjective 'He and I could not stop talking.'

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'My sister told my mom that her phone had run out of battery. She borrowed a charger from a neighbor. Later, it stopped working again during the movie.' The writer means that my sister's phone died and the sister borrowed the charger. Rewrite the passage so 'her,' 'She,' and 'it' all have clear references, and explain the ambiguities.
items.answer: 'My sister told my mom that my sister's phone had run out of battery. My sister borrowed a charger from a neighbor. Later, the phone stopped working again during the movie.' The original 'her' and 'She' could mean the sister or the mom, and 'it' had no clear noun, so naming 'my sister' and 'the phone' makes each reference clear.

steps: 'her phone' is ambiguous: it could be the sister's phone or the mom's phone. The intended meaning is the sister's, so write 'my sister's phone.'
'She borrowed a charger' could mean the sister or the mom. The writer means the sister, so name her: 'My sister borrowed a charger.'
'it stopped working' has no clear noun nearby (charger or phone?). The writer means the phone, so write 'the phone stopped working.'
When two people or two objects could match a pronoun, replace the pronoun with the exact noun to remove all doubt.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Me and the other volunteers planted trees along the river on Saturday. The park ranger gave the saplings to Tara and I to carry. When a volunteer plants a tree, you feel proud of yourself.' Rewrite the passage to fix the two case errors and the shift in person, and explain each change.
items.answer: 'The other volunteers and I planted trees along the river on Saturday. The park ranger gave the saplings to Tara and me to carry. When volunteers plant a tree, they feel proud of themselves.' The first sentence needs the subject 'The other volunteers and I,' the second needs the object 'Tara and me' after 'to,' and the third must stay third person plural with 'volunteers... they... themselves.'

steps: Sentence 1: 'Me and the other volunteers' is the subject of 'planted,' so use 'The other volunteers and I planted.'
Sentence 2: 'to Tara and I' follows the preposition 'to,' so use the objective 'to Tara and me.'
Sentence 3 shifts from singular third person 'a volunteer' to second person 'you... yourself.' Make it consistent plural third person: 'When volunteers plant a tree, they feel proud of themselves.'
'Themselves' here is correct as a reflexive pronoun because the volunteers feel proud of the volunteers.

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'Carlos and Diego studied together for the history exam. He explained the timeline of the revolution to him. After the test, his teacher praised the way he had prepared.' The writer means that Carlos explained the timeline to Diego, and that the teacher praised Carlos. Rewrite the passage so the references are clear, and explain why the original is confusing.
items.answer: 'Carlos and Diego studied together for the history exam. Carlos explained the timeline of the revolution to Diego. After the test, Carlos's teacher praised the way Carlos had prepared.' The original 'He,' 'him,' and 'he' could each refer to Carlos or Diego; replacing them with names matches the intended meaning and removes the confusion.

steps: Both boys are named first, so 'He explained... to him' is ambiguous: either Carlos or Diego could be the explainer or the listener.
Use the intended meaning: Carlos explained the timeline to Diego.
Replace the pronouns with names: 'Carlos explained the timeline of the revolution to Diego.'
The last sentence's 'he had prepared' is also unclear; the writer means Carlos, so write 'Carlos's teacher praised the way Carlos had prepared.'

items.prompt: Read the passage: 'The new students themselves designed the welcome posters for the hallway. Mrs. Lopez told the students and I that them posters looked professional. Between you and I, the artwork was better than anything me and my friends made last year.' Rewrite the passage so every pronoun follows standard English, and explain which pronoun in the passage was already correct and why.
items.answer: 'The new students themselves designed the welcome posters for the hallway. Mrs. Lopez told the students and me that those posters looked professional. Between you and me, the artwork was better than anything my friends and I made last year.' 'Themselves' was already correct as an intensive pronoun emphasizing 'students'; the other pronouns needed fixing for case ('me'), determiner use ('those'), and the objective 'between you and me,' plus the subject 'my friends and I.'

steps: 'The new students themselves designed' is already correct: 'themselves' is an intensive pronoun emphasizing 'students' and can be dropped without breaking the sentence.
'told the students and I' makes the pronoun the object of 'told,' so use the objective 'the students and me.'
'them posters' misuses an object pronoun as an adjective; use the demonstrative 'those posters.'
'Between you and I' must be objective after the preposition 'between': 'Between you and me.' Finally, 'me and my friends made' is the subject of 'made,' so use 'my friends and I made.'
